PullRequest.Title: eslint: fix bracket notation in workbench services
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- replace identifier-safe bracket notation across the 23 allowlisted Workbench UI and remaining service files
- remove the cleaned group from `.eslint-allowed-bracket-notation-files`
- replace private-member bracket access in default-account tests with a typed test subclass and protected production seams

Stacked on #334756.

## Validation

- targeted ESLint: 24 changed source files
- targeted hygiene: 24 changed source files
- exact-scope audit: 23 removed allowlist entries plus one typed test-support file
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run transpile-client`
- `node --check src\vs\workbench\contrib\webview\browser\pre\service-worker.js`
- policy export integration: 2 passing
- encoding integration: 3 passing
- default account unit tests: 49 passing
- editor utilities/options unit tests: 15 passing
- update info parser unit tests: 21 passing
- workspace tags unit tests: 3 passing
- extension recommendations unit tests: 143 passing

## Known baseline drift

The Color Registry release test reports 1 passing and 2 failing checks because the generated known-variable list and `theme-color.md` are out of sync with currently registered colors and sizes. This PR does not include those unrelated generated/documentation updates.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup and configuration/theme/menu registration, including editor option validation, accessibility delay lookup, localization labels, menu rendering, and extension theme construction
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Synchronous in-memory property reads and existing fixed-size option verifier construction occur on registration/configuration paths; no changed operation crosses a process or I/O boundary. Theme and menu work remains on the same pre-existing activation/render paths.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Editor validation has a fixed set of options; menu rendering scales with contributed commands and theme construction scales with loaded theme contributions, exactly as before the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous local work; no queue, limiter, parallelism, or backpressure behavior is changed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing configuration, contribution, and theme registries remain authoritative; no cache key, lookup, invalidation, warm/cold behavior, or negative caching changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the complete hunks only replace identifier-safe bracket access with dot access while preserving verifier, loop, and constructor placement.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact activation frequency varies by feature use, but every changed access is semantically the same own/inherited JavaScript property operation and adds no work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression; work cardinality, allocation, and critical-path placement are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Interactive UI state changes and previews: call/type hierarchy peeks, bulk edit state, replace preview URI decoding, theme quick pick discrimination, walkthrough/editor telemetry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Hierarchy and bulk-edit changes perform the same single dataset write per state transition; replace preview performs the same JSON parse before resolving the same model reference. No geometry reads, forced layout, extra rendering, or newly awaited work is introduced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the existing source text model for a replace preview through createModelReference
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One model reference per opened replace-preview model, with the resolver's existing model reuse; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same model reference was created after decoding the same scheme from the same JSON query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The reference must resolve before preview content is available, but the changed JSON property access adds no boundary or delay.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One property write per widget state transition and one query parse per replace-preview model resolution; hierarchy tree size and search result size are unaffected.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI writes and parsing remain synchronous; existing asynchronous model resolution remains unchanged and no coalescing or cancellation semantics move.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No widget, model, preview, or telemetry cache lifecycle is changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed widget methods and full replace-preview call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual hierarchy refresh and preview-open frequency varies, but there is no changed multiplicity or boundary behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding; dot access preserves the same DOM/model work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Usage-telemetry workspace classification and Azure/dependency tag discovery during workbench activation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The contribution launches reporting without awaiting it on startup. Tag discovery performs existing filesystem existence checks, folder resolves, and selected manifest reads; the changed lines only assign tag fields or read parsed dependency fields.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve node_modules and inspect root folder entries for workspace telemetry tags
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resolveAll call containing one resource per workspace folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical resolveAll and scanning; only tags['node'] became tags.node.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous telemetry work, off the UI startup critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check/read pom.xml and other dependency manifests per workspace folder
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one existence/read pair per applicable manifest per workspace folder after root-name gating; existing Promise.all grouping is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical checks, reads, parsing loops, and concurrency; only identifier-safe parsed/tag properties use dot notation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before the corresponding telemetry tags are emitted, but does not block workbench progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check and optionally read aiGeneratedWorkspaces.json, then resolve workspace roots
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existence check, at most one read, and one resolveAll containing all folders per cold tag resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same files were checked/read and folders resolved before assigning tags['aiGenerated'].
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for getTags completion and telemetry reporting, not UI progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Filesystem work scales with workspace folder count: node_modules is resolved as one resolveAll group, Java checks use up to one pom existence/read per folder, and dependency manifests use existing per-folder reads only when root names indicate a candidate. Effective cardinality is unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Remote and Java folder checks use existing Promise.all fan-out; Azure node discovery precedes Java discovery; dependency manifest reads are aggregated in one Promise.all. No concurrency limit or burst size changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: WorkspaceTagsService retains its existing resolved tags promise/value; no cache key, invalidation, or cold/warm behavior changes. File service caching is used exactly as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from constructor activation, tag ownership, and complete filesystem call flow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large multi-root workspaces can make the pre-existing telemetry scan substantial, but this PR neither increases cardinality nor moves it onto a hotter path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Read and edit workspace extension recommendations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Recommendation queries read the workspace configuration first, then read folder .vscode/extensions.json files in parallel; toggles perform the same reads before user selection and writes. The changed parse result access occurs after the same workspace file read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read workspace configuration and per-folder extensions recommendation files
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One workspace read plus F folder reads for F workspace folders per invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The exact same files were read with the same serial/parallel schedule before extracting parse(... )['extensions'].
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Reads must complete before recommendations or toggle state are available.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One workspace configuration read when present plus one extensions config read per workspace folder; effective cardinality and deduplication are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The workspace read remains serialized before a Promise.all over folder reads; selected edits remain sequential in the existing loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The service still rereads on each public query/toggle and emits invalidation events on relevant file changes; this PR changes no caching or coalescing behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from all callers and the private resolver body.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Invocation frequency depends on recommendation consumers, but the changed line cannot alter read frequency or payload size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding; only equivalent local property access changed.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The export waits for extension/configuration registration, then obtains distro product data, serializes all policy data, writes one output file, and exits. The changed environment/product accesses remain in the same serial critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read DISTRO_PRODUCT_JSON when provided, otherwise read package.json; write generated policy data
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Environment branch: one input read and one output write. Fallback: one package read and one output write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same environment checks selected the same reads and output write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All are on the explicit export command's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch distro product.json from the GitHub contents API on the fallback branch
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one request per fallback export, with no retries or fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same one request was issued after reading process.env['GITHUB_TOKEN']; dot access does not alter branch selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks policy merging and output generation when no local distro product path is supplied.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Exit the native host after export success or failure
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One exit IPC/native call per export.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Terminates the one-shot process after output completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: CPU/serialization scales with registered policies and distro extension policies; boundary cardinality is fixed per export and unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Registration waits, distro retrieval, processing, output write, and process exit remain serialized; no concurrency burst or new await is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each one-shot export performs a cold retrieval; there is no cache before or after the diff. The environment-variable branch still avoids package-file and network retrieval.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete export and retrieval path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Policy catalog size affects existing serialization cost, but none of the changed accesses affects iteration count or bytes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Issue submission with GitHub attachment upload
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Repository ID resolution issues one GitHub API request when required; the submission-scoped closure memoizes the result, and existing file uploads proceed sequentially. The changed line only writes the Authorization field using dot notation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch GitHub repository metadata to resolve its numeric ID
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one lookup per applicable submission after submission-local memoization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same URL, request, headers, response parsing, and call count were used with headers['Authorization'].
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before attachments can be uploaded to the target repository.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequential IPC call per attachment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unchanged and not reached differently by the header assignment rewrite.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Uploads block completion of attachment processing.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One repository lookup per applicable issue submission, regardless of attachment count; upload count scales with attachments exactly as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Repository lookup is coalesced by the submission-local repoId variable; uploads remain sequential in uploadViaMobileApi. No burst or scheduling change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The repository ID is cached only for the lifetime of one submitIssue call; no cache key/lifetime change is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from submitIssue memoization and the native upload service implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Attachment sizes and network latency vary, but the PR changes neither bytes nor request count.

Scenarios.Scenario: Webview resource loading through the service worker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each matching GET/HEAD request checks CacheStorage, sends the existing load-resource message to parent client(s), awaits the host response, and optionally tees the stream into CacheStorage. The changed ETag assignment constructs an identical response header.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Post a load-resource request to each resolved parent webview client and await the host response
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One message per resolved parent client per matching resource request; effective parent-client fan-out is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical request-store, message, semaphore, and response flow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The host response is required before the resource response can complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Host-side resource load reached by load-resource IPC
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical host resource load per service-worker request, subject to the unchanged conditional-cache validation path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The ETag header was already emitted and sent as ifNoneMatch; bracket-to-dot assignment does not change host loading.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required on cold loads and validation requests; cached 304 responses reuse CacheStorage.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Clone/tee response streams and write cacheable responses to CacheStorage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cache put per successful cacheable GET resource response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical response headers, stream tee, cache put, and finalization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The response stream proceeds concurrently with the cache stream; finalizer ownership remains unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with webview resource requests and the number of matching parent clients; one cache match and one request-store entry occur per cache-eligible request, unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing host-response semaphore, independent service-worker fetch handlers, parent-client message fan-out, and stream finalizers are unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold requests still receive/store ETag responses; warm requests still forward cached ETag as ifNoneMatch and reuse cached responses on 304. Cache names, keys, puts, matches, and negative behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the full fetch dispatch, cache lookup, IPC, stream, and cache-put path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Resource volume varies widely by webview, but request cardinality, bytes, cache eligibility, and synchronization are invariant across the diff.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete 23-file inventory and every diff hunk under the performance focus. Production changes are identifier-safe bracket-to-dot property accesses with identical runtime work; the lone behavior correction is confined to a release test. Traced UI, startup, telemetry, recommendation, export, issue-upload, and webview-resource scenarios, including their filesystem/network/IPC boundaries, cache ownership, cardinality, and concurrency. No actionable diff-introduced performance issue or qualifying regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
